instructionSteps.description: >**NOTE:** This connector uses Azure Functions to connect to the Azure Blob Storage API to pull logs into Microsoft Sentinel. This might result in additional costs for data ingestion and for storing data in Azure Blob Storage costs. Check the [Azure Functions pricing page](https://azure.microsoft.com/pricing/details/functions/) and [Azure Blob Storage pricing page](https://azure.microsoft.com/pricing/details/storage/blobs/) for details.

>**(Optional Step)** Securely store workspace and API authorization key(s) or token(s) in Azure Key Vault. Azure Key Vault provides a secure mechanism to store and retrieve key values. [Follow these instructions](https://docs.microsoft.com/azure/app-service/app-service-key-vault-references) to use Azure Key Vault with an Azure Function App.

>**NOTE:** This data connector depends on a parser based on a Kusto Function to work as expected [**MuleSoftCloudhub**](https://aka.ms/sentinel-MuleSoftCloudhub-parser) which is deployed with the Microsoft Sentinel Solution.
**Note: This data connector fetch only the logs of the CloudHub application using Platform API and not of CloudHub 2.0 application**

**STEP 1 - Configuration steps for the MuleSoft Cloudhub API**

 Follow the instructions to obtain the credentials.

1. Obtain the  **MuleSoftEnvId**, **MuleSoftAppName**, **MuleSoftUsername** and **MuleSoftPassword** using the [documentation](https://help.mulesoft.com/s/article/How-to-get-Cloudhub-application-information-using-Anypoint-Platform-API).
2. Save credentials for using in the data connector.

**STEP 2 - Choose ONE from the following two deployment options to deploy the connector and the associated Azure Function**

>**IMPORTANT:** Before deploying the MuleSoft Cloudhub data connector, have the Workspace ID and Workspace Primary Key (can be copied from the following).

**Option 1 - Azure Resource Manager (ARM) Template**

Use this method for automated deployment of the MuleSoft Cloudhub data connector using an ARM Tempate.

1. Click the **Deploy to Azure** button below. 

	[![Deploy To Azure](https://aka.ms/deploytoazurebutton)](https://aka.ms/sentinel-MuleSoftCloudhubAPI-azuredeploy)
2. Select the preferred **Subscription**, **Resource Group** and **Location**. 
> **NOTE:** Within the same resource group, you can't mix Windows and Linux apps in the same region. Select existing resource group without Windows apps in it or create new resource group.
3. Enter the **MuleSoftEnvId**, **MuleSoftAppName**, **MuleSoftUsername** and **MuleSoftPassword**  and deploy. 
4. Mark the checkbox labeled **I agree to the terms and conditions stated above**. 
5. Click **Purchase** to deploy.

**Option 2 - Manual Deployment of Azure Functions**

 Use the following step-by-step instructions to deploy the MuleSoft Cloudhub data connector manually with Azure Functions (Deployment via Visual Studio Code).

**1. Deploy a Function App**

> **NOTE:** You will need to [prepare VS code](https://docs.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/functions-create-first-function-python#prerequisites) for Azure function development.

1. Download the [Azure Function App](https://aka.ms/sentinel-MuleSoftCloudhubAPI-functionapp) file. Extract archive to your local development computer.
2. Start VS Code. Choose File in the main menu and select Open Folder.
3. Select the top level folder from extracted files.
4. Choose the Azure icon in the Activity bar, then in the **Azure: Functions** area, choose the **Deploy to function app** button.
If you aren't already signed in, choose the Azure icon in the Activity bar, then in the **Azure: Functions** area, choose **Sign in to Azure**
If you're already signed in, go to the next step.
5. Provide the following information at the prompts:

	a. **Select folder:** Choose a folder from your workspace or browse to one that contains your function app.

	b. **Select Subscription:** Choose the subscription to use.

	c. Select **Create new Function App in Azure** (Don't choose the Advanced option)

	d. **Enter a globally unique name for the function app:** Type a name that is valid in a URL path. The name you type is validated to make sure that it's unique in Azure Functions. (e.g. MuleSoftXXXXX).

	e. **Select a runtime:** Choose Python 3.11.

	f. Select a location for new resources. For better performance and lower costs choose the same [region](https://azure.microsoft.com/regions/) where Microsoft Sentinel is located.

6. Deployment will begin. A notification is displayed after your function app is created and the deployment package is applied.
7. Go to Azure Portal for the Function App configuration.

**2. Configure the Function App**

1. In the Function App, select the Function App Name and select **Configuration**.
2. In the **Application settings** tab, select ** New application setting**.
3. Add each of the following application settings individually, with their respective string values (case-sensitive): 
		MuleSoftEnvId
		MuleSoftAppName
		MuleSoftUsername
		MuleSoftPassword
		WorkspaceID
		WorkspaceKey
		logAnalyticsUri (optional)
> - Use logAnalyticsUri to override the log analytics API endpoint for dedicated cloud. For example, for public cloud, leave the value empty; for Azure GovUS cloud environment, specify the value in the following format: `https://<CustomerId>.ods.opinsights.azure.us`.
4. Once all application settings have been entered, click **Save**.

instructionSteps.title: 1. Deploy the receiving resources
instructionSteps.description: Select Deploy to provision the receiving resources and obtain the configuration values below. Deployment does not configure MuleSoft applications or start forwarding logs. Your sender needs an Entra access token and Monitoring Metrics Publisher access on the DCR. See the [Logs Ingestion API overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-monitor/logs/logs-ingestion-api-overview).

parameters.content: Deploy the Log Analytics table, Data Collection Endpoint (DCE), Data Collection Rule (DCR), and Entra application with ingestion permissions.

parameters.label: Deploy MuleSoft CloudHub Logs receiving resources

parameters.content:
### Sender configuration

Copy these values into your compatible appender or external collector. The DCR value below is its immutable ID, not its ARM resource ID. Use Entra application credentials, not MuleSoft Connected App credentials.

parameters.text: Store the client secret in protected application or collector configuration. Do not hardcode it in log4j2.xml or include it in logs.

instructionSteps.title: 2. Configure application log forwarding
instructionSteps.description:
1. Choose a custom asynchronous Log4j appender that supports Azure Monitor Logs Ingestion, or send logs to an external collector that implements it. No ready-made sender is supplied with this connector; a generic HTTP appender alone does not implement Entra token refresh or schema mapping.
2. Add the appender dependency to your Mule application's `pom.xml` and configure `src/main/resources/log4j2.xml` using that appender's instructions. Repeat for each application, or use your deployment automation. Follow the guide for your platform: [CloudHub 1.0](https://docs.mulesoft.com/cloudhub/custom-log-appender) or [CloudHub 2.0](https://docs.mulesoft.com/cloudhub-2/ch2-integrate-log-system). Do not use the 1.0 file/appender configuration unchanged on 2.0.
3. Configure the sender with the tenant ID, client ID, protected client secret, DCE URL, DCR immutable ID and stream name from step 1. It must acquire and refresh an Entra token with scope `https://monitor.azure.com/.default`, then POST a JSON array to `{DCE}/dataCollectionRules/{DCR-immutable-ID}/streams/Custom-MuleSoftCloudhubLogs_CL?api-version=2023-01-01` with `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and `Content-Type: application/json`.
4. Map records to the DCR fields: `EventTime` (UTC timestamp), `Level`, `Logger`, `Message`, `Thread`, `Exception`, `ApplicationDomainName`, `InstanceId`, `WorkerId`, `Environment`, `Region`, and `ApplicationData` (JSON object). Configure batching, retry/backoff and delivery monitoring in the sender. See [Logs Ingestion API examples](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-monitor/logs/tutorial-logs-ingestion-code).
5. Deploy a test application and verify forwarding before rolling out to other applications or disabling existing logging.

instructionSteps.title: 3. Verify ingestion
instructionSteps.description:
Generate a uniquely identifiable test log and confirm its message and application context in `MuleSoftCloudhubLogs_CL`:

```kusto
MuleSoftCloudhubLogs_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| project TimeGenerated, ApplicationDomainName, Level, Message
| take 10
```

If the record is missing, inspect sender delivery errors: check the Entra token for 401, DCR permissions for 403, and the stream name and JSON field types for 400. Confirm connectivity to the DCE and token endpoint. Receiving-resource deployment alone does not confirm end-to-end ingestion.

dataFlows.transformKql: source | extend TimeGenerated = iff(isnull(EventTime), now(), todatetime(EventTime)) | project TimeGenerated , EventTime , Level , Logger , Message , Thread , Exception , ApplicationDomainName , InstanceId , WorkerId , Environment , Region , ApplicationData

schema.name: MuleSoftCloudhubLogs_CL
schema.description: MuleSoft CloudHub application logs streamed in real-time via Log4j HTTP appender. Contains standard Log4j fields plus MuleSoft-specific context and flexible custom application data.

columns.name: EventTime
columns.description: Timestamp when the log was generated

columns.name: Level
columns.description: Log level (INFO, WARN, ERROR, DEBUG, FATAL)

columns.name: Thread
columns.description: Thread name that generated the log

columns.name: ApplicationData
columns.description: Customer-specific application data in JSON format

schema.name: MulesoftCloudhubAlerts_CL
schema.description: Mulesoft CloudHub alerts from the CloudHub API v2

columns.name: CreatedAt
columns.description: Timestamp when the alert was created (Unix epoch milliseconds)

columns.name: LastModified
columns.description: Timestamp when the alert was last modified (Unix epoch milliseconds)

columns.name: IsSystem
columns.description: Whether this is a system-generated alert

columns.name: Condition
columns.description: Alert condition configuration including type, resources, and resource type

columns.name: Actions
columns.description: Alert actions configuration including notification settings

connectorUiConfig.title: Mulesoft CloudHub Alerts Connector (via Codeless Connector Framework)
connectorUiConfig.descriptionMarkdown: Ingest CloudHub 1.0 alerts into Microsoft Sentinel using the CloudHub REST API v2. CloudHub 1.0 entitlement is required; API v2 does not mean CloudHub 2.0. This connector does not collect CloudHub 2.0 alerts or on-premises Runtime Manager alerts. Use a Connected App with OAuth2 client credentials (recommended), or Basic authentication where supported by your organization. Configure the regional Anypoint Platform URL, environment ID and optional application filter. The alert list is polled every five minutes; previously returned alerts may be ingested again. Use the optional deduplication query when needed. See [CloudHub API documentation](https://docs.mulesoft.com/cloudhub/cloudhub-api) and [Connected Apps documentation](https://docs.mulesoft.com/access-management/creating-connected-apps-dev).

sampleQueries.description: Deduplicate repeated CloudHub alert revisions (last 24 hours)
sampleQueries.query:
let alerts = MulesoftCloudhubAlerts_CL | where TimeGenerated > ago(24h);
union
(alerts | where isnotempty(Id) and isnotnull(LastModified) | summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by OrganizationId, EnvironmentId, Id, CreatedAt, LastModified, Name, Severity, ProductName, Enabled, IsSystem, _ConditionKey = tostring(Condition), _ActionsKey = tostring(Actions) | project-away _ConditionKey, _ActionsKey),
(alerts | where isempty(Id) or isnull(LastModified))

| where TimeGenerated > ago(6h)

| where isnotempty(Time)

instructionSteps.title: 1. Mulesoft CloudHub Connections
instructionSteps.description: Manage connections to your Mulesoft CloudHub environments

parameters.content:
## Prerequisites

1. Your organization must have **CloudHub 1.0 entitlement**. A 403 response stating that this entitlement is not enabled cannot be fixed by changing credentials. CloudHub 2.0 is not supported by this connector.
2. For **OAuth2 (recommended)**, create a Connected App under **Access Management > Connected Apps** with **App acts on its own behalf (client credentials)**. Grant **Runtime Manager > Read Alerts** for the target business group and environment. Save the app and use its client ID and secret, not the environment's client ID/secret.
3. For **Basic**, use an Anypoint username/password only if Basic API authentication is supported for that account. Do not use Connected App credentials in Basic mode.
4. Find the environment ID under **Access Management > Business Groups > Environments**. The environment must match the Read Alerts scope assignment.

See [Connected App setup](https://docs.mulesoft.com/access-management/creating-connected-apps-dev).

parameters.text: This connector requires CloudHub 1.0 entitlement and Read Alerts access. API version v2 is not CloudHub 2.0. Contact your MuleSoft administrator to confirm product entitlement.

parameters.label: Add Connection
parameters.title: Add Mulesoft CloudHub Connection
parameters.subtitle: Configure a connection to a Mulesoft CloudHub environment

instructionSteps.title: Base Configuration
instructionSteps.description: Configure your Mulesoft CloudHub API connection

parameters.text: Enter a unique alias to identify this connection. Use descriptive names like 'US-Production', 'EU-Staging', etc.

Enter your regional Anypoint Platform HTTPS URL, for example https://anypoint.mulesoft.com, https://eu1.anypoint.mulesoft.com, or https://gov.anypoint.mulesoft.com. The connector resolves /cloudhub/api/v2/alerts and the OAuth token endpoint on this origin. An existing URL ending in /cloudhub/api also works. Do not enter an application URL or a custom proxy path.

instructionSteps.description: Select authentication, then provide the matching credentials

instructionSteps.description: Configure the CloudHub environment to monitor

instructionSteps.title: 2. Monitor and Validate
instructionSteps.description: Monitor data ingestion and validate connectivity

parameters.content:
### Monitor and Validate

- Alerts are polled every five minutes from `/cloudhub/api/v2/alerts`, with offset pagination, and stored in `MulesoftCloudhubAlerts_CL`. `MuleSoftCloudhub` is the parser, not the table.
- **401**: Verify the selected authentication method, credentials and API region.
- **403**: Inspect the vendor error. Check CloudHub 1.0 entitlement and Read Alerts permission for the requested environment.
- **Non-JSON response / 404**: Verify the regional Anypoint Platform URL, not a login page or application URL.

### Repeated Alerts

This endpoint returns an alert list. No verified time-window filter is configured. The five-minute polling interval does not limit results to newly created alerts. Previously returned rows may be ingested again.

Use the optional **Deduplicate repeated CloudHub alert revisions** sample query. It compares organization, environment, alert ID, revision timestamps and payload fields, keeping the latest collected copy; alert updates remain separate. Rows without an ID or last-modified timestamp are retained without deduplication. This is query-time deduplication only: it does not delete rows or reduce ingestion charges. Raw-table queries and existing parser consumers remain unchanged.

This connector does not collect CloudHub 2.0 alerts or on-premises Runtime Manager alerts. Use a Connected App with OAuth2 client credentials (recommended), or Basic authentication where supported by your organization. Configure the regional Anypoint Platform URL, environment ID and optional application filter. The alert list is polled every five minutes; previously returned alerts may be ingested again. Use the optional deduplication query when needed. See [CloudHub API documentation](https://docs.mulesoft.com/cloudhub/cloudhub-api) and [Connected Apps documentation](https://docs.mulesoft.com/access-management/creating-connected-apps-dev).

sampleQueries.description: Deduplicate repeated CloudHub alert revisions (last 24 hours)
sampleQueries.query:
let alerts = MulesoftCloudhubAlerts_CL | where TimeGenerated > ago(24h);
union
(alerts | where isnotempty(Id) and isnotnull(LastModified) | summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by OrganizationId, EnvironmentId, Id, CreatedAt, LastModified, Name, Severity, ProductName, Enabled, IsSystem, _ConditionKey = tostring(Condition), _ActionsKey = tostring(Actions) | project-away _ConditionKey, _ActionsKey),
(alerts | where isempty(Id) or isnull(LastModified))

instructionSteps.title: 1. Mulesoft CloudHub Connections
instructionSteps.description: Manage connections to your Mulesoft CloudHub environments

parameters.content:
## Prerequisites

1. Your organization must have **CloudHub 1.0 entitlement**. A 403 response stating that this entitlement is not enabled cannot be fixed by changing credentials. CloudHub 2.0 is not supported by this connector.
2. For **OAuth2 (recommended)**, create a Connected App under **Access Management > Connected Apps** with **App acts on its own behalf (client credentials)**. Grant **Runtime Manager > Read Alerts** for the target business group and environment. Save the app and use its client ID and secret, not the environment's client ID/secret.
3. For **Basic**, use an Anypoint username/password only if Basic API authentication is supported for that account. Do not use Connected App credentials in Basic mode.
4. Find the environment ID under **Access Management > Business Groups > Environments**. The environment must match the Read Alerts scope assignment.

See [Connected App setup](https://docs.mulesoft.com/access-management/creating-connected-apps-dev).

properties.descriptionHtml:
Note: Please refer to the following before installing the solution:

• Review the solution Release Notes

• There may be known issues pertaining to this Solution, please refer to them before installing.

The MuleSoft Cloudhub solution provides the capability to ingest logs from Cloudhub applications into Microsoft Sentinel. This solution includes two data connector options: an Azure Function-based connector using the Cloudhub API, and a push-based CCF connector that receives logs directly via Log4j HTTP appender as recommended by MuleSoft.

Underlying Microsoft Technologies used:

This solution takes a dependency on the following technologies, and some of these dependencies either may be in Preview state or might result in additional ingestion or operational costs:

  1. Codeless Connector Framework (CCF)

  2. Log Ingestion API

  3. Data Collection Rules (DCR)

  4. Azure Monitor HTTP Data Collector API

  5. Azure Functions

Data Connectors: 3, Parsers: 1
